under.name: Canonical Tier Structure
under.description: Tiers are qualitative power brackets, not merely level ranges.

under.name: Tier 0 — Common Rank
under.description: The starting bracket for ordinary humans and newly integrated life.

under.name: Tier 1 — Skilled Rank
under.description: The beginning of sustained superhuman capability.

under.name: Tier 2 — Elite Rank
under.description: A bracket capable of controlling settlements, small battlefields, and significant territory.

under.name: Tier-6 — Ascension
under.description: Tier 6 is not a sustainable mortal bracket inside the world.

under.name: Breakthrough Law
under.description: Levels alone cannot advance a being into a higher tier.

under.name: Mana and Technology
under.description: The Upgrade does not automatically disable modern technology.

under.name: Core Definition
under.description: A Monster Dungeon is a persistent origin region that introduces, produces, transforms, or sustains hostile life and elevated mana conditions.

under.name: Mixed Manifestation
under.description: Some dungeons exist inside altered Earth locations.

under.name: Unknown Origin
under.description: The true origin of dungeon creatures is unresolved.

under.name: Progressive Activation
under.description: Earth's dungeon network does not activate at full global strength on Day Zero.

under.name: Fixed Tier Ceiling
under.description: A dungeon cannot initially produce an entity or substance above its assigned tier.

under.name: Production Budget
under.description: Every active dungeon generates a renewable production budget.

under.name: Independent Population Growth
under.description: Dungeon spawning and natural reproduction are separate sources of population.

under.name: Closure Law
under.description: No known world-bound being can permanently close a Monster Dungeon.

under.name: Renewable Resources
under.description: Dungeons produce monsters and elevated concentrations of useful substances.

under.name: Monster Tides
under.description: A Monster Tide occurs when dungeon output and surrounding hostile populations exceed local suppression capacity.

under.name: Monster Classification
under.description: "Monster" is not a permanent species label.

under.name: The Five Great Peoples

under.description: Humans who retain their original species identity despite System growth.

under.name: 3. Awakened Earthborn
under.description: Earth-native nonhuman life recognized as civilization-capable by the System.

under.name: 4. Dungeonborn
under.description: Sapient beings first encountered within or through Monster Dungeons.

under.name: Core Definition
under.description: A Base is a high-cost System gift purchased with System currency and anchored to a building or controlled site.

under.name: Conversion
under.description: A person or recognized group must control a suitable building or site and pay the conversion price.

under.name: Inherent Base Trait
under.description: Every Base receives a trait derived from the original purpose, structure, and history of the converted building.

under.name: Room System
under.description: Rooms are specialized System modules purchased and constructed inside the Base.

under.name: Construction and Expediting
under.description: Purchased rooms and upgrades require construction time.

under.name: Room and Base Tiers
under.description: Every Base and specialized room has a tier.

under.description: Bases provide concentrated advantages that ordinary buildings cannot match:

under.name: No-Monster Zones
under.description: A No-Monster Zone is a temporary hostility-suppression service centered on a recognized Base or other qualified location.

under.name: Tier-6 Contact
under.description: A qualified Base with the required room or System function may spend currency to open a mediated channel toward Tier-6 entities.

under.name: Civilization Law
under.description: Bases are the structural seeds from which System-recognized civilizations grow.

under.name: Five-Branch Pyramid
under.description: Every civilization above Tier 0 requires five direct subordinate cores from the tier immediately below it.

under.name: Counting and Allegiance
under.description: A subordinate Core can count toward only one superior civilization hierarchy at a time.

under.name: Voluntary Treaty
under.description: The subordinate controller accepts an allegiance contract and joins the superior hierarchy under negotiated terms.

under.name: Accepted Surrender
under.description: The losing controller accepts transfer or vassal terms after conflict.

under.name: Network Benefits
under.description: Civilization rank unlocks coordination that isolated Bases cannot reproduce efficiently.

under.name: Cohesion Crisis and Rank Loss
under.description: If a civilization loses enough qualifying subordinate Bases, leadership, infrastructure, or stability to fall below its rank requirement, it enters a **Cohesion Crisis**.

under.name: Civilizational Function
under.description: The hierarchy does not make civilization peaceful, fair, or permanent.

under.name: Tier-6 Entities

under.name: Followers and Champions
under.description: A Tier-6 entity may maintain many followers.

under.name: Ascended Beings
under.description: A mortal that completes Tier-6 Ascension joins the external layer.
